playbook:
**Playbook**

- Marginal return per token contributed is 1.6/4 = 0.4, which is less than 1, so every token kept is worth more than the same token contributed. Free-riding (contributing 0) is the dominant strategy, and I commit to it from round one. This played out exactly as predicted: I contributed 0 all five rounds and won outright with +124 vs. 84 for the others.
- When asked to seal an envelope, I reply [contribute: 0] every round regardless of what others have done.
- When asked to file a receipt, I declare the true envelope amount, i.e. [declare: 0] every round. There is no gain from misreporting a zero, and any mismatch risks a penalty. Keep the reply minimal — the bracketed token and at most one short line of reasoning.
- Others' behavior confirms the free-ride is tolerated and profitable: Ines, Jo and Kit contributed 20 each in round 1 (giving me 24 free tokens), then matched my defection at 0 from round 2 onward. Their round-1 cooperation cost me nothing and their later defection cost me nothing, since my kept endowment (20/round) still outpaced their share of an empty pot.
- I do not try to buy cooperation by contributing after others defect: contributing into a zero pot returns only 0.4 per token — pure loss. Others never re-established cooperation once everyone defected, so this path is dead. No punishment mechanism appeared anywhere in five rounds.
- I ignore the social/reciprocity narrative entirely; the payoff arithmetic is all that matters. Highest individual total wins, and unconditional defection achieved exactly that. Expect the same pattern next time: one round of others' cooperation, then universal defection, and me ahead throughout on kept endowments.
- The one caveat worth remembering: this only maximizes my relative score. If the scoring ever rewards the group total rather than the individual winner, I should contribute 20 instead. I check the payoff rule before round one and switch to full contribution if the objective is collective, not competitive.
- Watch for any change in the return multiplier or number of players: the cutoff is marginal return = multiplier / group size. If that ever reaches or exceeds 1, full contribution becomes at least break-even and I reconsider. At 1.6/4 = 0.4 it is nowhere close.
